DateBound.description:
An inclusive date window, or a named relative preset.

Bounds accept ISO-8601 dates (`"2024-01-01"`) or Elasticsearch date math
(`"now-30d"`, `"now/M"`). Both bounds are inclusive — `gt`/`lt` deliberately
do not exist on the wire.

DiscoverFilters.description:
Every filter accepted for `category: company` and `category: person`.

Names match prism's filter vocabulary exactly — this is a contract mirror,
not a re-design, so a name that reads oddly (`gov_nongov`) stays as it is
rather than being prettied up into something prism would reject.

Which side a filter applies to is not encoded here: prism routes a
person-side filter through `has_child` when the search targets companies
(and vice versa), so `seniority` is meaningful on a company search. The one
honest statement this model can make is which filters *exist*.

that many countries. Prism refuses a place it does not know with `request.invalid`.

PersonRecord.description:

instead of the thin stub in the job history. The complete parent record
